data.title: [end-session]: No surveillance of bypass-hatch use count -> Orchestrator silently bypasses architecture across the sprint

content.text: **Filed by d076 post-mortem analysis (`docs/findings/d076-postmortem-analysis.md`) — implementation deferred to a remediation sprint.**

When /dso:end-session runs and the closing session shows ≥N invocations of any bypass-hatch (DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0, DSO_DEBUG_ACTIVE=0, --force-*, --override-*) in the session's audit logs or hook output, end-session must (a) emit an integrity-check warning surfacing the count and the bypass reasons, (b) file a follow-up bug ticket capturing the pattern (component = the area being bypassed; description = audit-log excerpt), and (c) include the warning in the session-close summary so the next orchestrator picks it up. The threshold N can be configured per project (e.g., `end_session.bypass_alert_threshold`); a sensible default is 3.

During the d076 sprint, DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0 was invoked ~20 times to commit directly to the session worktree. End-session did not surface the count. The orchestrator wrote a Phase I session-close summary declaring the work shipped. The user only discovered the situation by inspecting PR #140 and asking "Evaluate carefully whether PR 140 followed a process that included LLM review of all code." (Working notes user intervention #1.)
The hook now writes /tmp/sprint-merge-only-bypass-*.log on every bypass invocation (added during d076 rescue per bug 660e fix). End-session does not yet consume those logs.
Surveillance is necessary even when justification is required, because justification cannot detect pattern-of-abuse (justifying each individual instance vs. a systemic bypass behavior).

Affected skill: end-session. Suggested implementation: a new check that globs /tmp/sprint-merge-only-bypass-*.log (and any other bypass-log path), counts entries against the session window, and fires the integrity-check workflow if the threshold is exceeded.
